root_idea.summary: The root centers on thickness, density, or coarseness, with figurative extensions to hardness, roughness, severity, and strength.
root_idea.development: The physical idea of thickness is extended to abstract qualities: roughness in conduct, severity in punishment, strength of a covenant, and forcefulness in confrontation.

senses.definition: To be rough, harsh, or stern toward others; to use roughness in dealing with them.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranically used in the imperative construction وَٱغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ, directing forceful or stern conduct toward opponents.

senses.definition: To become thick, dense, and well-grown.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic plant image, the seed-produce becomes thick and robust; the form can also convey becoming prepared for that condition.

senses.definition: Harsh or rough in disposition; stern or hard-hearted.
senses.usage_conditions: Applied to a person or to character and conduct; the Quranic contexts include sternness in disposition and the description of stern beings.
Used in Quranic descriptions of punishment and torment.
Used of a compact or covenant, especially one treated as firmly binding.

senses.definition: Hardness, strength, or vehemence shown in enmity and fighting; forceful resistance.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic command, it concerns confronting hostile opponents with firmness, endurance, and force.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become thick, gross, bulky, or coarse; of a body, garment, or other physical thing, and also of rough or rugged land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the general physical use of the Form I verb, distinct from the Quranic Form X description of growing vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thick, gross, big, bulky, or coarse; also rough or rugged, especially of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical adjective applied to bodies, cloth, and comparable things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thickness, grossness, bulkiness, or coarseness; also physical roughness or ruggedness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These nominal variants are attested as substantives derived from the physical sense of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rough or rugged land or ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare and lexicographically disputed noun; some authorities repudiate it or treat it as related to غَلِيظٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dense or deep in color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the intensity or depth of a color.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become hard or difficult, of an affair; by analogy, to be gross or grave, of a crime.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The application to a crime is reported as analogical rather than as an independently transmitted usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hard or difficult, of an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application of the adjective to circumstances or matters that are difficult to deal with.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make or render something thick, gross, bulky, or coarse; figuratively, to make it hard or difficult.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II is causative and may describe making a matter difficult for someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an oath strong, forcible, confirmed, or ratified; to be rigorous or severe in an oath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with an oath or in administering an oath.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mutual opposition carried on with roughness or hostility; mutual enmity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III verbal noun describing reciprocal antagonism.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find a garment or piece of cloth thick or coarse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Some reports extend the expression to buying cloth in that condition, but finding it thick or coarse is the preferred interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To alight, or to alight and remain, in a rough or rugged tract of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form IV use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be rough, harsh, coarse, rude, or ungentle toward someone in speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with في القول; this speech-related construction is distinguished from the Form II expression غَلَّظَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To regard something as thick, gross, bulky, or coarse; to refrain from buying cloth because of its thickness or coarseness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Form X evaluative or transitive use, distinct from the Quranic inchoative use with vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Roughness, coarseness, rudeness, unkindness, hardness, or incivility in manners, conduct, or speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is the opposite of رِقَّة in social behavior and disposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hardness or difficulty of an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative nominal use for circumstances that are difficult or severe.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hostility or enmity between parties.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction describing hostility between two sides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Severe or vehement, of slaying or wounding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical extension of the adjective to violent acts; it is not treated as a separate Quranic object restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bitter, of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative application of the adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An aggravated bloodwit or fine for bloodshed, made legally more severe than an ordinary compensation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical legal expression for compensation due in specified aggravated or intentional homicide circumstances.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The thick part of the forearm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical noun.

The rare Classical noun غَلْظٌ meaning rough land is retained, but the supplied lexicographic evidence records disagreement about its validity.
